answer: Each agent must complete a small, randomly assigned task whose answer is checked against a hidden reference before it can earn reputation or claim a scarce market role. The task changes over time, so copying one response across many identities fails; creating accounts alone brings no advantage. An attacker must spend compute and time solving each challenge, while honest agents reuse established reputation. A lantern task about juniper growth might unlock access to a haven of trusted sellers, but every new identity must qualify on its own.
